notice: Easy Mode dramatically simplifies the process of filter selection, an otherwise nuanced topic. Only a few of HQPlayer's filters are accessible here, so think of Easy Mode like training wheels and don't be afraid to experiment.

help.title: Easy Mode, explained
help.body:
Select Playlist for a mix of content quality and sources back-to-back, or Album for consistent production and quality, then pick your preset and its emphasis or version.

Choose 'Space' for live or acoustic performances where the room or venue is part of the recording. These filters emphasize accuracy in the upper octaves where our ears perceive spatial cues.

Transients are sudden sounds: a snare drum hit, or the leading edge of a plucked string. Choose 'Transients' for most multi-track studio recordings; such content often has an artificial sense of space that doesn't rely on the highest frequencies, but does have strong transient content like percussion. These filters emphasize the clean reproduction of such sudden events.

Note that the effect of these levers varies from preset to preset: for example, 'The Purist' adjusts the filter's length to change the emphasis; Old School, on the other hand, changes its phase.

'Hi-Res' modes are optimized for material with a sampling rate ≥88.2 kHz rather than any 24-bit content. These modes also work for lossy material like MQAs and MP3s. 'Auto' uses the correct filter automatically for lossless content; set to 'Hi-Res' for lossy material.

The glyphs (A) and (1/2) indicate the error correction level (apodizing); if no or half error correction sounds harsh or generates an apodizing events warning, try a different setting.

Still can't decide? Experiment! Presets can be changed live at any time with only a brief interruption to playback.

perfect-ten.title: The Perfect Ten
perfect-ten.description: Does everything well, no strings attached: the best-case solution to the tension at the heart of filter design. Start here.

lifelike.title: Lifelike
lifelike.description: Puts the focus on natural, realistic timbre. Excellent with live performances.

lossy.title: Lossy Mode
lossy.description: Make the most of lossy playlists, streams, or files such as MQA or MP3.

old-school.title: Old School
old-school.description: Best for classic-era analog recordings. Try it with modern content, too!

purist.title: The Purist
purist.description: Passes the original samples through unchanged. Only recommended for the highest technical quality source material.

damage-control.title: Damage Control
damage-control.description: Aggressive clean-up for loudness war-era and other less-than-good material.

concert-hall.title: The Concert Hall
concert-hall.description: Heavily emphasizes space at the cost of transients. For material with minimal transients like live classical.
